messages.subject: Mentor voting on proposals
parts:
Over the next week mentors should be reviewing proposals and applying votes to those where
they consider they are knowledgeable. Please simply pass when you are not "in the field"
sufficiently to give a good appraisal.

Note from the timeline that the deadline is April 20.

April 20:
* All mentors must be signed up and all student proposals matched with a mentor - 07:00 UTC
* Student ranking/scoring deadline. Please do not add private comments with a nonzero
score or mark students as ineligible (unless doing so as part of resolving duplicate
accepted students) after this deadline - 17:00 UTC
* IRC meeting to resolve any outstanding duplicate accepted students - 19:00 UTC

R got 16 slots tentatively. We have about 17 reasonable proposals, which is not too bad,
but there will obviously be some discussion about ranking.

Some serious matters:

1) Mentors: Please put PRIVATE comments with your voting. Tell us why the proposal should
or should not be funded. Are there changes which would make it better?

2) Mentors: Use gsoc-r to ask questions, but do NOT put comments on proposals there --
students can see them.

3) All: Some proposals have already been "ignored". This is because the admins have judged
that they do not have sufficient support or chance of succeeding. Sometimes this is
because the student is too inexperienced. Sometimes we don't have mentors. Sometimes the
project is too ambitious. If there is serious interest from the MENTORS, one or two may be
revived. But sorry, students don't get to vote. We had 55 proposals this year, up from 40
last year.

4) We do need mentors -- as per policy developed over the last year (with R-core input),
we will require at least 2 mentors per proposal to get a slot. But if you are willing to
mentor, do tell us who you are and your qualifications for the task. And we also want you
to be on this list -- pity we are having trouble with a couple of folk who have applied on
Melange to mentor, but who are not getting this. And we really don't want to be sending
private emails to EVERY mentor candidate. Students -- you can ask people you know who may
be willing to mentor to apply to gsoc-r list and Melange GSoC interface, telling us who
they are and their qualifications and interest.

We also will not let one person be primary mentor to more than one project, but they can
be backup on another, preferably just one other. Besides avoiding the nasty situation that
a report is not filed and a student does not get paid (nearly happened last year when
mentor was travelling and out of communications), more mentors widens the R development
community.

Hope that covers everything (but I'm sure it won't!)

Best, John Nash
